_comment: The honest ledger of what this suite actually exercises versus what it is still waiting for.
IntegrationReadinessTests reads this file and enforces it in BOTH directions:
status = 'pending'  -> the path/marker must still be ABSENT. If it has appeared, the test
FAILS, because a pending test must not quietly stay pending after
the code it was waiting for lands. A [Fact(Skip=...)] is invisible
the moment its blocker clears; this is not.
status = 'landed'   -> the path/marker must still be PRESENT. Once wired up, the same entry
becomes a regression guard, so the ledger keeps earning its keep
instead of decaying into a to-do list nobody re-reads.
Flip status in the same change that wires the test up, and move the entries out of 'blocks'
into 'covers' as they are genuinely covered.

note: The workflows present are squad automation and an SDK pin guard — none of them build
or test any .NET project. Every guarantee in this suite currently
depends on somebody running `dotnet test` by hand. A test suite that is not wired into
a gate is a suggestion, and this is the single largest gap in Phase 1 assurance.
